standfirst: Jeju, a photographer whose career collapses in public, and the weather forecaster who has loved her since childhood. The back half is excellent and the per-episode ratings climb every week to prove it. Getting there means seven hours of a Seoul scandal plot the writing does not care about.

picks.why: The same island, doing more with it. Jeju as an economy and a set of family obligations rather than scenery, with a haenyeo culture that is treated as work. Difference: it is an anthology, so no single couple carries it and no episode is padded.

City woman, seaside village, a man everybody already trusts. The template Samdal-ri is working in, executed with a tighter script and a warmer ensemble. Difference: the male lead's grief is the actual plot, so the back half deepens instead of resolving.

A hometown that will not stop talking about you. Both are about a woman returning to a place that has already decided who she is, and both make the gossip a real antagonist. Difference: a serial killer thread runs underneath it, which gives every warm scene a floor of dread.

Childhood friends, mothers who are best friends, and a career failure nobody wants to admit. Nearly the same premise from the next year, right down to the return home in disgrace. Difference: the mothers get equal screen time, and the show is honest that the parents caused most of it.

Two lives, one hometown, and the question of who got to leave. Same interest in what a small place does to ambition, and the same slow, kind pacing. Difference: the central relationship is between sisters, and it is far more rigorous about work.

An island, a dream deferred, and a comeback nobody is rooting for yet. Same 2023 warmth and the same trust that a competent woman rebuilding is enough. Difference: the premise is high concept, and the family violence in it is handled bluntly.

against.title: When Life Gives You Tangerines
against.why: Recommended because it is also Jeju and also about families. It is a four-decade portrait of poverty and loss that will wreck you. Samdal-ri is a romance with a village attached.

against.title: Hospital Playlist
against.why: The reflex comfort pick. There is no hometown, no returning failure and no childhood promise in it; the pleasure is competence among friends, which is a different appetite.

against.title: Once Upon a Small Town
against.why: Named as the generic countryside romance. It is much slighter, and it has none of the family history that makes Samdal-ri's second half work.
